audits.finding: The canonical major relationship inventory and the 21 audit both retain R001 through R012 with matching relationship IDs and bounded from/to semantics.

The 20 graph audit reports 48 source edges, while the canonical normalized graph has 49 after the disclosed N-PLANET-SURFACE supporting node and E-052 edge. This is an intentional normalization difference, not an unexplained count contradiction.

The canonical provenance says E-007, E-030, and E-047 were corrected, but their current endpoints still conflict with their descriptions and the 20 audit resolutions: E-007 is content-to-world while its description says world-to-content, E-030 is PropertyList-to-configuration while configuration consumes PropertyList, and E-047 is registry-to-save while the description says save-to-registry reconstruction.

The asserted and unresolved endpoint overlaps are separated by relation type in the canonical graph, including identity lookup versus name derivation, gameplay consequence versus transport ABI, and presentation reference versus complete asset semantics. The event enqueue/dispatch pair remains qualified rather than promoted to a universal ABI.

The 20 audit identifies a legacy-byte-level to semantic-package crosswalk as an open normalization action. The canonical package inventory does not claim that crosswalk is complete, but a final report must not compare package counts across namespaces without preserving that qualification.

asset_relationship_consistency.finding: Relationship IDs and bounded relationship statements agree, but the canonical graph still contains three direction defects that contradict the controlling graph-audit disposition.

contradictions.finding: Canonical provenance claims that E-007, E-030, and E-047 direction semantics were corrected, but the current canonical edge endpoints remain E-007 N-CELL-CONTENT to N-CELL-WORLD-DATA, E-030 N-PROPERTY-LIST to N-CONFIGURATION-DATA, and E-047 N-OBJECT-REGISTRY to N-SAVE-DATA, while the descriptions state the opposite dependency directions.

Canonical semantic gap MR-003 still says the graph has no direct PlanetData-to-surface or PlanetData-to-presentation edge, but the canonical graph contains E-021 N-PLANET-DATA to N-PLANET-SURFACE and E-052 N-PLANET-SURFACE to N-PRESENTATION-DATA. MR-003 is stale as a current missing-semantic claim after the disclosed normalization.
The 19 audit records all 18 data-model inputs as untracked and the canonical provenance repeats that disclosure, while the 21 audit says it read all 18 committed data-model artifacts.

The 19 contradiction entry says DM12 records both 0x008E0D30 and 0x008E1000. The 0x008E1000 SDK-named RegisterDatabase entry is in DM01, while the selected DM12 registry manager evidence uses 0x008E0D30; the address-kind distinction is plausible, but the DM12 attribution is not.

The canonical high_centrality entries contain the same node IDs, ranks, degrees, and packages as the 20 ranked list, but canonical array order is rank 1, 10, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9 while the controlling graph audit presents numeric rank order 1 through 10. Values agree; consumer-visible order is not normalized consistently.

audits.finding: The canonical synthesis inventories 21 artifacts, including DM19-DM21. Each of the three final audit documents scopes its worker input set to DM01-DM18. This is an intentional staged-audit scope difference and is explicitly consistent with the canonical precedence policy.

audits.expectation: The final report plan does not lose or rename the 11 canonical report points.
audits.finding: The 21 plan contains the first 11 sections with titles and requirement IDs matching the canonical FR-01 through FR-11 records, then explicitly adds FR-12 through FR-16 for comparison slices, package questions, prohibited claims, and determinism.

audits.expectation: Required counts agree across canonical and mission coverage.

audits.finding: The canonical 32-node set matches the 20 graph node set and the 21 RM-04 inventory. N-PLANET-SURFACE is separately disclosed as a supporting analytical node rather than silently substituted for a canonical node.
R001 through R012 occur in both canonical and 21 inventories. The 21 wording is a bounded paraphrase of some canonical endpoints, not a new relationship claim.

audits.expectation: The canonical graph implements the direction corrections required by the 20 audit.

The canonical synthesis adds a qualified derived flow using the same edge path and marks transport as unresolved and runtime validation as not established. This is an intentional normalization, but the derived-flow distinction should remain explicit.

audits.expectation: Graph gaps are not retained as current missing semantics after their edges are added.
audits.finding: E-021 and E-052 now provide the direct PlanetData-to-surface and surface-to-presentation path, so MR-003's literal missing-edge claim is stale. The runtime transition remains unresolved and must not be promoted.

audits.expectation: Address and function-kind claims retain the correct source attribution.
audits.finding: The distinction between the 0x008E0D30 vtable entry and the 0x008E1000 SDK-named RegisterDatabase body is compatible with the available source artifacts, but the 19 entry incorrectly says DM12 records both. The address-kind distinction is sound; the source locator is not.

The canonical six-level vocabulary is CONFIRMED, INFERRED, OBSERVED_CURRENT, SUPPORTED, UNKNOWN, and VERIFIED. The audits explicitly qualify these as bounded static or current evidence and prohibit promotion to original runtime truth.

The 57 DC classifications in canonical persistent_vs_transient_state exactly match DM17 data_classification: 18 static asset/template, 15 runtime transient, 14 profile/save persistent, 6 unknown, and 4 derived/cache.

audits.expectation: Persistence layers, save/load entry points, and missing status agree.

The complete persistence package remains missing/prerequisite rather than covered.

audits.expectation: OpenSpore comparison classifications and counts agree.
audits.finding: Canonical and 21 agree on 72 items: 10 represented, 10 partial, 20 missing, 20 incorrect, and 12 intentional-modern-divergence.

audits.expectation: Intentional divergence is separate from missing or incorrect semantics.
audits.finding: The 12 DIV items are a distinct classification with an explicit current-host effect and no equivalence claim. They are not folded into the 20 missing or 20 incorrect items, and 21 retains the same five-way grouping.

audits.expectation: Different missing-reference results are not conflated.
audits.finding: The 19 audit reports two missing dossier paths and five stale ranges in its broad reference scan. The 20 audit reports zero missing source paths in the 16 graph source only. These are different scopes and are consistent when the scan boundary is stated.

audits.expectation: Deterministic-order claims agree with the actual array presentation.

The 19 audit also records a determinism failure for input arrays and anchor vocabularies. Determinism must be disclosed rather than stated as unqualified success.

audits.expectation: The final review remains read-only and does not mutate source, Ghidra, SPORE, or historical artifacts.
audits.finding: The three final audits all declare read-only mutation boundaries. This review likewise only creates the requested review output and does not alter the audited inputs or any code, Ghidra database, SPORE content, or historical artifact.

Final consistency is blocked by graph-direction defects, stale graph-gap wording, one provenance-status contradiction, and one address-source attribution error.

eleven_point_coverage.finding: The canonical campaign and executive summary contain the same ordered 11-point report set. The 21 mission audit preserves all 11 as its first 11 planned sections and adds five explicitly labeled supplemental sections.

evidence_level_consistency.finding: Evidence labels are consistent with the canonical policy and are not promoted to original runtime, save/load, ABI, or pixel equivalence.

checks.finding: The 72-item classification counts agree exactly: 10 represented, 10 partial, 20 missing, 20 incorrect, and 12 intentional-modern-divergence.
Intentional divergence is explicitly a current OpenSpore design difference with no original-equivalence claim; it is not used as a substitute for missing or incorrect original semantics.
